standard.title: Develop, practise and refine aural and instrumental skills
standard.description: develop, practise and refine listening/aural skills and style-specific vocal/instrumental skills
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have developed ensemble listening skills, vocal and instrumental techniques for expressive effect, and used digital tools for skill development (AC9AMU8D01 — Y7-8). They can make real-time ensemble adjustments and monitor technique using recordings. The Y9-10 step adds: identifying challenging sections and building stamina, mapping and realising dynamic interpretations, and developing technical and expressive facility and control at a higher level.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop, practise and refine listening/aural skills and style-specific vocal/instrumental skills, demonstrating increasing technical and expressive facility and control.

nodes.label: Identifying challenges and building stamina
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the technically or musically challenging sections in music they are learning, develop targeted strategies for those sections, and build the stamina to perform the whole work.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two challenging sections in a piece being prepared; develop and apply a different targeted strategy for each.
nodes.typical_width: Systematically identify challenges across a piece — technical challenges (speed, range, coordination), musical challenges (expressive nuance, stylistic conventions), and stamina challenges (maintaining quality across the full work); develop and apply targeted practice strategies for each; monitor progress and adjust strategies as needed.
wider: Document a practice log over a rehearsal period — record challenges identified, strategies tried, and progress observed; use the log to inform subsequent practice
Focus specifically on stamina: identify where quality drops across a full-length performance and develop conditioning strategies targeted at those points
nodes.hinge_reason: Self-directed practice — identifying challenges and developing strategies without teacher direction — is the foundational skill of independent musicianship. Students who cannot identify and address their own technical weaknesses remain permanently dependent on teacher diagnosis. This is the defining difference between a student who improves in teacher-led rehearsal and one who improves between sessions.

response_modes.reason: Build the diagnostic habit explicitly: before each practice session, students identify one specific challenge to work on, one strategy to try, and how they will know if it worked. After the session, brief reflection: 'Did the strategy work? What did you discover?' This moves practice from running-through to deliberate improvement.

success_criteria: Can identify at least two technically or musically challenging sections in a piece being prepared
Has applied a targeted strategy for each and can describe what they tried and what changed

nodes.label: Ensemble skills and collaborative listening
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can work collaboratively to develop ensemble skills — listening carefully to establish and maintain balance, intonation and blend across parts.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one real-time ensemble adjustment (balance, intonation or blend) made in response to listening to other parts; describe what was heard and how the adjustment was made.
nodes.typical_width: Work collaboratively in ensemble contexts to develop balance, intonation and blend — listen for specific parts, adjust dynamics and tuning in real time, respond to other performers' expressive choices; compare ensemble sound across different configurations (duo, trio, larger ensemble).
wider: Record an ensemble rehearsal, listen back together and identify three specific moments where balance or intonation was an issue — develop targeted strategies for each and re-record
Compare ensemble challenges across different ensemble sizes (duo vs quartet vs larger group) — describe how listening demands change with ensemble size

response_modes.reason: Ensemble listening at Y9-10 requires the individual performance skills to be sufficiently fluent that full attention can go to the group sound. Consolidation here means structured ensemble rehearsal formats that explicitly ask students to monitor specific aspects (balance this rehearsal, intonation next rehearsal) rather than general ensemble playing.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Ensemble experience across different configurations (duo, trio, chamber, larger ensemble) develops different listening and balance skills — each configuration is genuinely distinct as a musical experience.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one real-time ensemble adjustment (not prompted by teacher) during collaborative performance
Can describe what they heard and how they adjusted in response

nodes.label: Mapping and realising a dynamic interpretation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can map a planned dynamic interpretation for a piece (identifying loudest and softest points, shaping dynamic arcs) and practise to realise the plan in performance.
nodes.minimum_width: Map the dynamic plan for one section of a piece — identify the loudest and softest points and the shape between them; practise to realise the plan and compare a recording with the intended plan.
nodes.typical_width: Map a full dynamic interpretation plan for a complete piece — analyse another performance for comparison, identify where the plan differs from default, practise to realise the plan, compare before/after recordings and evaluate the degree of realisation.
wider: Compare dynamic interpretations of the same piece by two different performers — describe how each shapes the dynamic arc differently and what each interpretation communicates
Map a planned interpretation, realise it in performance, then try a contrasting interpretation — compare which communicates the music more effectively and justify the preference

response_modes.reason: Dynamic mapping makes an interpretive plan visible and testable. The teaching investment is in establishing the habit: plan the interpretation before rehearsing it, then use recording to evaluate the degree to which the plan was realised. This creates a feedback loop between intention and execution that builds expressive control.

success_criteria: Produces a dynamic interpretation plan for a section or full piece
Can compare a recording of the performance against the plan and describe where the plan was realised and where it was not
